findings.bottleneck_verdict: WITHDRAWN AND REPLACED. The 'co-limited, not purely memory bound' reading below was a residual, not a decomposition, and the ablation behind it was unsound: it folded the row stage's plane store into four addresses, which does remove the device_memory write traffic but also serialises the store pipe on aliased addresses, so the stage became store-issue-bound (18.674 ms) and the 1.71 ms 'saving' cannot be read as a device_memory share. Re-measured without aliasing in experiments/20260916-ssb-mps-colimit (row_store_width.py: same instruction count, same tiled order, only the stored element width changed), halving the write bytes recovers 4.531 ms of 20.755 ms, i.e. 54.5% of the pure-device_memory prediction, so the write traffic is real but about half-overlapped. The '6.27 ms intermediate device_memory prize, 17% of the fit' is therefore withdrawn. What still stands here is the byte accounting, the refutation of accumulate-first, and the threadgroup-capacity block on fusing the two stages.
findings.bottleneck_verdict_superseded_by_colimit: The 8937-BF fit is co-limited, not purely memory bound. The objective moves 87.01 GB of modelled traffic in 643.4 ms = 135.2 GB/s against a 131.1 GB/s same-session 1:1 copy control, but the stage ablations show device_memory is not what binds: removing the row stage's 2,147 MB plane write saves only 1.71 ms of 20.38 ms and removing the column stage's 2,147 MB plane read saves 4.56 ms of 17.82 ms. The row stage's mixed ceiling is 196.2 GB/s (1:4 write-heavy control) yet it runs at 131.8 GB/s, so roughly 60-70% of each stage's time is non-device_memory cost (correction ALU, butterfly issue/barriers at 32 KB threadgroup occupancy). The intermediate round trip is still the largest single byte item - 4,295 MB of 4,834 MB per pack, 88.9% - and it is worth about 17% of the fit wall, but it is not removable: fusion needs the whole plane on chip, and moving the sum is refuted by the objective's own nonlinearity.
findings.fit_change_verdict: f357069 (tiled scalar row IFFT, bit-exact, 1.093x end-to-end on the scalar loss and 1.081x on the isolated stage pair) does not touch the fit path and must not be quoted as a fit result: the fit calls _reconstruct_prepared_batch_exact_loss, a 4-trial fit calls _reconstruct_prepared 0 times and the batched row IFFT 1944 times (18 packs x 108 objectives), and the batched path was already tiled in the frozen 32ba29b tree (tiled_output=batch<=2 and tiled_input=batch<=2 at engine.py:3005-3010 and 5042). Tiling is a lossless address permutation, so there is no byte saving to apply there. The paired fit A/B delta (79.28 -> 77.72 s p50) is host drift.
findings.intermediate_prize_withdrawn: The 6.27 ms figure (1.71 ms row store + 4.56 ms column read) is withdrawn as a device_memory share. The row half came from an aliasing-unsound ablation; the column half came from a read-pinned variant that removes device_memory read traffic but keeps the load instructions, so it measures the overlapped share, not the traffic. Superseded by experiments/20260916-ssb-mps-colimit.
findings.next_levers_if_the_pinned_value_may_move: Only two, and both need a recapture decision: (a) a fused single-kernel row+column stage, which this hardware cannot host (64x over the measured 32,768 B threadgroup limit) and which would be worth about 17% of the fit wall as an upper bound on its device_memory share; (b) any other butterfly ordering, priced at 8e-7 relative on the pack loss against the engine's own 1.2e-7 float32 floor.
ranking: 1. engine.py:4975 pack loop -> engine.py:2626 tiled row store -> engine.py:2337 tiled column load: the intermediate round trip, 4,295 MB of the 4,834 MB moved per 512-BF pair pack (88.9%) and, by ablation, 6.27 ms of the ~35.7 ms per pack (17% of the 79.0 s fit). Blocked, not recoverable.
2. engine.py:2660/2712 G_qk read inside the row kernel: 539 MB per pack shared across the pair, 11.2% of a pack's bytes and 20.1% of a single candidate's.
3. engine.py:5080 Nelder-Mead: 31 sequential batch-1 evaluations, 14.4% of the fit, unamortisable because the simplex is sequential; the 200-trial loop (83.4%) is already batch-2.
4. Row-stage non-device_memory cost: 18.67 ms of 20.38 ms survives with the plane write folded; the row stage's own mix ceiling is 196 GB/s against 131.8 GB/s achieved.
5. Column-stage non-device_memory cost: 13.26 ms of 17.82 ms survives with the plane read pinned; atan2 ablation was already measured at 5%.
rejected: Accumulating the candidate-weighted BF planes in the frequency domain and transforming once (IFFT linearity, proposed as IFFT2(sum_bf c_bf G_bf) == sum_bf IFFT2(c_bf G_bf)): refuted on the objective, not on precision. The loss is mean_pixel(Var_bf(phi)), a variance of the phase across BF terms, so a phase must exist per BF term; the atan2 sits between the transform and the sum and sum_bf phi_bf != phi(sum_bf z_bf). A second independent barrier is that the Nyquist boundary correction is added inside the atan2 argument and is indexed by BF term. The redraw path legitimately accumulates first because its output really is linear; that is why the idea looked general. Independently refuted by the Metal agent.

Fusing the row and column stages into one kernel so the intermediate round trip disappears (4,295 MB of the 4,834 MB per 512-BF pair pack): blocked by on-chip capacity, measured here rather than assumed. The threadgroup ceiling on this host is 32,768 B (33,792 B refuses to load with 'Threadgroup memory size (33792) exceeds the maximum threadgroup memory allowed (32768)') and both engine kernels already reserve exactly 32,768 B, while the transformed plane is 2,097,152 B = 64x that. The only tile that fits, 512 rows x 8 columns, needs 64 threadgroups each re-reading the full input: 64x input amplification. A hypothetical version that removed the intermediate's device_memory traffic entirely would save 6.27 ms of the ~35.7-37.0 ms per pack (17%), i.e. 79.0 s -> about 65.6 s at 8937 BF, and it would change the butterfly ordering and move the pinned loss by about 8e-7 relative.

paper.claim: The 8937-BF exact-objective fit on MLX/MPS moves 87 GB per batch-2 objective at the machine's streaming ceiling and is co-limited by non-device_memory stage cost; the row-IFFT intermediate is its largest byte item but cannot be removed on this hardware or by reordering the linear sum.

ablations.note: A strict lower bound on the fused prize: the variants keep every store and load instruction and only remove the device_memory traffic, so a real fused kernel would save this much or more - but it cannot be built on this hardware.

fused_kernel_requirement.argument: A single fused row+column kernel must hold the transformed plane per threadgroup (2,097,152 B against a measured 32,768 B limit). Splitting the second stage by output columns fits exactly at 512 rows x 8 columns x 8 B = 32,768 B, but each of the 64 groups then has to transform 8 output columns of every one of the 512 rows, so it reads the full 2,097,152 B input instead of 1/64 of it: 64x the current per-plane input traffic.

mix_controls.note: The row stage's read:write mix allows 196 GB/s but it runs at 131.8 GB/s, so the row stage is not at its own device_memory ceiling; the column stage (read-heavy, ceiling 127.0 GB/s) runs at 120.5 GB/s and is closer to it.
